items.note: The HMS-TT-ADD-LN2 option is a passive LN2 bath: the user pours LN2 into the reservoir/funnel and the sample sits in a flooded bath (catalog: 'Hold time is approximately 10 min'). There is no cryocooler and no documented cooldown/pull-down time; the configuration has no cooldown concept. Snapshot 052e125d6ba34edd checked.

Pan et al. (NIST pub 931816, snapshot d74643f3f5552cfa) describe the PT405 cryogen-free cryostat and the 12-day runs and 8-12 h stabilization after each pressure change, but give no time from room temperature to operating temperature. The custom LNE-Cnam cryostat has no manufacturer cooldown specification. Not estimated.

Cryostat-100 is an LN2 boil-off calorimeter whose cold mass is filled with LN2 by the operator (phases: cooldown/fill, cold soak, steady-state boil-off). It has no cryocooler and no machine cooldown specification; the cold-soak duration depends on the insulation specimen and no Cryostat-100-specific figure was found (NTRS 20150011030, NTRS 20130012853, insulation.org article checked; the '>= 24 h' and '8 h' figures found belong to other apparatus: sleeved cryostat / Cryostat-P100).

items.quote: The cool-down takes approximately three to four (3-4) hours from the time the compressor is turned on.
items.note: Quantum Opus Opus One manual, Cool Down Procedure: base is 'typically below 2.5 K' on Stage 2 (the NASA paper also reports 2.5 K). Upper bound of the 3-4 h range taken. The FAQ (https://www.quantumopus.com/documentation/faqs) gives 'about 4 hours ... depending on your vacuum pump'; product page advertises 'One-Button, 3-hour Cooldown' for one-button models. Procedure is for a fully warm system (>280 K).

The LOCR is a custom liquid-helium-cooled radiometer (built by Cambridge Research & Instrumentation to NIST specification). Neither the 2001 comparison paper (PMC4862825, snapshot d8e16b89ccfd2107) nor web/NIST searches gave a cooldown time or LHe fill-to-operation time. Not estimated.
NPL cryogenic testing services page (snapshot d9514a42ec8a494b) describes helium cooling with active temperature control for 20 K tests but states no cooldown time; no other NPL source found.

items.quote: cool down time (incl. pumping time) | < 4.5 h to 5 K (depending on thermal load)
items.note: attocube attoDRY800 specification table. Time is to 5 K (guaranteed base), including pumping; the Thomas 2024 setup operates at 4 K. attocube defines cooldown time as start of automated cooling to guaranteed base temperature, and states it can deviate with microscope/magnet configuration (the in-cryostat objective and piezo stack add load). The RT-SWD shroud page gives '4.5 .. 5.5 h' to T<5 K for that shroud variant; the shroud used by Thomas 2024 is not identified, so the general spec is used.

Wiens et al. 2020 (arXiv 2004.01552v3, snapshot 7fcceddad2c0642d) mention cooling to 4 K then to 1.5 K and a deliberate '15-day-long slow cool-down' from 22 K used for CTF measurement, which is not a room-temperature-to-base cooldown. No Leiden Cryogenics CF-1K datasheet with a cooldown time was found. Not estimated.

Linkam pages and brochure (THMS600, LNP96, T96, McCrone, UMCS brochure v1.1) give cooling rate (100 C/min max with LNP96) and range to -196 C but no stated time to reach the low set point. Deriving a time from the rate would be an estimate, so none is given.
Heating-only configuration (no LNP96 pump): the stage cannot cool below ambient, so there is no cooldown or pull-down to an operating temperature.
THMSEL600 pages (features/specifications) and LNP96 page give range and rates but no time to reach low temperature. Not estimated from the cooling rate.

items.quote: System cooldown 60 hours from room temperature to 4 K
items.note: Oxford Instruments TeslatronPT brochure (Wayback copy; the live URL now redirects to QD Oxford, whose current pages give only the sample cooldown '< 2 h ... probe loaded into cold VTI'). System cooldown to 4 K; the archived Japanese product page (https://web.archive.org/web/2021id_/https://nanoscience.oxinst.jp/products/cryofree-magnets/teslatronpt) says '~ 60 hours ... (varies with different magnet options)'. Not specific to the 8 T magnet option; it is the brochure figure for the family. Sample space reaches < 1.5 K, so base is reached after this plus the probe cooldown.
